title: csv.DictReader
summary: Iterate a CSV file as dicts keyed by the header row.
description: Handles quoting, embedded commas, embedded newlines and escaping — all the things that make `line.split(',')` wrong.

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: An open file object. Open it with newline=''.

parameters.name: fieldnames
parameters.description: Use when the file has no header row.

parameters.name: restval
parameters.description: Value for keys missing from a short row.

returns: An iterator of dicts. **Every value is a string.**

examples.title: Read and convert at the boundary
examples.code: import csv\nwith open('s.csv', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:\n    total = sum(float(row['amount']) for row in csv.DictReader(f))

real_world_usage: Supplier feeds, exports, report inputs. Convert types once, on the way in, rather than at every point of use.

common_mistakes.fix: Produces blank rows between records on Windows.
One quoted field with a comma breaks it. Real CSV is full of them.

performance_notes: C-accelerated and streams row by row, so memory is constant. For millions of rows with heavy analysis, Polars or PyArrow are far faster.
security_notes: Beware CSV injection: a value beginning with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is executed as a formula when opened in a spreadsheet. Prefix untrusted values with an apostrophe when exporting.
